schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: THE HEARTBEAT, and all of it (Akien 2026-09-30, ticket bae622881f03): 'Not everything we MIGHT need, everything we KNOW WE NEED.' The resident runner (`python3 -m cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop`) (1) claims the singleton (guard.claim_singleton, an flock on <home>/run.lock held for the process's life); a second loop exits 3 while one is running and LIVE, and a holder whose record is DEAD is sent SIGTERM and the claim retaken once; (2) on start records the mtimes of its own top-level .py files (heartbeat.own_files/mtimes); (3) each beat compares them (heartbeat.changed), calls on_pulse(now, {}) on every groundloop/pulse.py found at class or instance level (discovery.pulse_sites; heartbeat.Triggers, which holds each module against its mtime and re-loads on change; one raising trigger never stops the rest), and writes ONE JSON — liveness.json: beat time, pid, and state {beats, started, recorded_mtimes, current_mtimes, changed, triggers} — which the pane and `cairn groundloop status` read; (4) COMMAND_EXIT.flag in <home> stops it; a changed own file re-execs it in place (os.execv of sys.orig_argv, same pid) unless COMMAND_DO_NOT_RESTART.flag is present. The menu of flags lives in <home>/flags/. THAT IS ALL. No bus, no probes, no shims, no web server launch, no import or bytecode checks. Each of those belongs to something else: mail and clock probes to the owning device (in its own pulse.py), event probes to the gate/door that fires them, the web server to its own shim. STILL STANDING BESIDE IT, NOT PART OF THE RUNNER: loop.py's in-process GroundLoopDevice (with staleness.py) is still constructed by bus_client/web_server — the sibling ticket moves those consumers off it; see filed_edges.
why: One heartbeat that every device hangs its own clock work on, so no device runs a bespoke daemon of its own (the UU disease: dozens of independent daemons rotting silently). It stays this small because every extra duty is a way for the one thing everything depends on to fail: measured 2026-09-30, a bytecode-staleness check misfiring under Python 3.14 restarted the loop 61 times on an untouched tree. The only questions a heartbeat needs answered are: has my own code changed, and whose trigger did I call.
invoke: Run resident: `python3 -m cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop` (superclaude spawns it as the systemd-run unit cairn-ground-loop; spawning it twice is safe — the loser exits 3). Operator: `cairn groundloop status|start|stop|restart` — status prints LIVE/DEAD, pid, beats, age, each trigger called with ok/FAILED, and a changed-files count. Stop: `touch <home>/COMMAND_EXIT.flag` or SIGTERM (an Event, so the wait is woken). Hold restarts while editing: copy flags/COMMAND_DO_NOT_RESTART.flag into <home>. Get beat service: put `groundloop/pulse.py` with `on_pulse(now, context)` at your class address or under ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<n>/. Prove: `python3 cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/proofs/test_heartbeat.py` (exit 0 = green).
entry: FRESH design to Form v0. The mechanism is Cairn's own: one daemon, one beat, firing-in-the-shim. No mechanism grafted.
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter — the charter-state-history split; this file stays pure intention+why, the operational voyage lives in the sidecars (Law 1/4/7)
filed_edges: (a) the in-process GroundLoopDevice (loop.py) and staleness.py still stand because bus_client connect_system and the web server construct one; the sibling ticket the-cli-and-web-server-reach-devices-without-a-private-ground-loop moves them off it, then both go.

(b) clock probes that lived in devices' probes/ folders move into each owning device's own groundloop/pulse.py, one ticket per device (Akien 2026-09-30); event probes belong to the gate or door that fires them, never the loop.
gates: proof gate (tester) — proofs/test_heartbeat.py, runnable bare (python3) and under the tester. Durability gate: not done until proven AND committed.
falsifier: RED on any of (proofs/test_heartbeat.py): (1) an own-file touch, addition or removal not named by changed(), or an untouched tree read as changed; (2) a pulse.py at class or instance level not called, a raising one stopping the others, or the beat's call list not in the record; (3) the record missing beats/started/recorded_mtimes/current_mtimes/changed/triggers; (4) a second runner starting while one is LIVE, or not exiting 3; (5) a changed own file not re-execing in place (same pid, new start), or re-execing while COMMAND_DO_NOT_RESTART is set; (6) COMMAND_EXIT not stopping it with rc 0, or the flags menu absent; (7) the runner re-growing anything else — a bus, a device, staleness, discovery of probes/, a takeover arbiter — or the loop's own probes/ holding a .py. Live horizon: the deployed loop beats past 3 with one pid and changed == [].
how_it_learns: It does not; it is the heartbeat — it records its own file times, calls the pulse files it finds, and writes what it did. Learning belongs to the devices whose triggers it calls.
traces_to: Law 1 (one daemon, folded once — not re-derived as a bespoke loop per device)
Law 4 (a single heartbeat is physics; every handler hangs on it)
Law 5 (intent + code + proofs share this address)
the converged architecture (CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-heartbeat-probes-and-bus.md — the heartbeat is the first of the two substrates)
cairn/tools/base/shim.py (the shim carries the per-pulse probe-firing — 'hang probes on it' built into all devices)
cairn/tools/base/probe.py (the immutable unit the shim fires — a trigger is any predicate, evaluated where owned)
CC memory [[cc-reify-vs-flow]] (the goof: three roles frozen into one device; the fix flowed them apart)
build order: db domain → ground loop → … (MAP.md:892)
owner: CC owns the ground_loop code + its proofs and gates writes to them. The heartbeat is the shared substrate every device's shim depends on; the probes hung on it are owned by their own devices (class-space declarations), and any durable state they touch is owned through db_domain.
proof: proofs/test_heartbeat.py — the heartbeat's teeth, written first and run RED at 81ac20e4 (every failure an absence): pure mtime/changed teeth over temp trees, trigger firing over class- and instance-level pulse trees with one raising, and the runner as a subprocess at a 0.3s cadence (record fields, second loop exits 3, DO_NOT_RESTART, re-exec same pid, COMMAND_EXIT rc 0, flag menu, nothing else). proofs/test_stop_is_prompt.py — SIGTERM wakes the wait. proofs/test_ground_loop.py, test_discovery.py, test_staleness.py, test_cli.py — the in-process GroundLoopDevice, liveness record, claim, pulse discovery and CLI, still standing for their consumers.
provenance: Born 2026-07-18 as the fifth spine step; reworked the same day from a driver-executor into the heartbeat. Grew a bus device, shims, probe discovery, bytecode staleness, takeover arbitration and six probes of its own through 2026-09. Cut back to the heartbeat 2026-09-30 (ticket bae622881f03) after the staleness check restarted it 61 times on an untouched tree under Python 3.14; the full trail is in git and the commons.
